findings.text: closure_wake_up offers a wake operation for a closure wait list that first enforces ordering for prior list updates and then delegates to the internal wake helper.
A thread waking a closure wait list must make earlier wait list modifications visible before the wake; the provided wake wrapper inserts the required barrier on the waker side.
The callback and container helpers define the conventional work callback shape and a means to recover the enclosing closure and then its outer object from the scheduled work item.

Closure continuations move by installing a next function plus workqueue and then either dropping a running reference or directly requeueing; distinct return forms encode plain termination versus termination through a destructor with different reference adjustments.
closure_call initializes a closure with an optional parent linkage and then schedules its first function on the supplied workqueue using the no-barrier continuation path.

The wait-for-event helpers test the predicate before waiting to avoid unnecessary sleep, otherwise repeatedly attach a stack closure to the wait list, retest the predicate, block until woken, and finish by waking peers and synchronizing once more.

The timeout wait variant derives a deadline from current time plus the requested interval, reports at least one tick when already satisfied, zero on expiry, and otherwise waits with a timed sync while recomputing the remaining interval.
Bounded unsigned ranges are pairs of base plus size in 32 and 64 bit widths, with defined unbounded sentinels starting at zero with maximal size and empty sentinels at maximal base and size.

A code tag records flag bits, source line, and module, function and file names with eight byte alignment; a reference union holds one tag pointer, a type descriptor holds section identity, tag size and module lifecycle callbacks, and an iterator holds type, module, tag cursor plus module identity and sequence state.
Code tag sections use fixed start and stop name markers, and one low flag bit denotes an inaccurate tag.

The default tag initializer captures the build module identity plus current function, file and line and clears flags; the module identity expands to the build module name or to null depending on configuration.
When module section support is absent the codetag module helpers report no section needed, allocation failure, and successful no-op load, unload, replace and free behavior.
Process event connectors for fork, exec, id change, session change, command change, ptrace, coredump and exit are present as empty inline no-ops in this configuration.
Compat system call definition macros generate per-arity compat entry points with a sanitized-argument secure alias, error injection annotation, and suppressed aliasing diagnostics around the wrapper.

Basic compat layouts include a vector entry of compat address plus length, an alternate signal stack of address plus flags plus size also named as compat stack type, process times of four clock values, and a signal set as a fixed array of compat words sized from the signal count.

Compat signal actions carry a handler address, flag word, optional restorer address and packed mask, with field order and restorer presence varying by architecture; the old action layout carries handler, old mask, flags and restorer.

Compat signal info carries signal number, error and code with architecture dependent code ordering, plus a large payload union for kill, timer, realtime, child, fault, poll and syscall cases, including fault subcases for trap number, address lsb, bounds, protection key and perf data.

Compat file locks describe type, origin, start, length and process identity with architecture selectable extra fields, padding and packing; compat resource limits hold current and maximum values and compat resource usage holds old timevals plus memory, fault, swap, block, message and context switch counters.

Further compat layouts cover directory entries, filesystem status, event notification with value plus signal plus notify method and a union for padding, thread id or thread routine, network interface map, settings, request and configuration structures, and robust futex lists with next linkage, futex offset and pending operation pointer.
Compat key derivation parameters carry compat addresses for hash name and other info plus an info length and reserved spare words.

Compat signal mask transfer copies between native and compat user masks with big-endian 64-bit word splitting when needed; unsafe put and get forms perform wordwise or bulk copying under caller managed fault handling.
The unsafe compat alt-stack saver stores the current task alternate stack address, flags and size into the supplied compat user structure.
Compat mode queries in these fragments report either the current compat task state or a constant false, with task compat checks and 64-bit alignment fixup need both constant false.
Compat pointer conversion widens a 32-bit compat address into a user pointer and truncates a user pointer back to 32 bits.

Compat time and identity helpers scale jiffies by compat user frequency, convert nanoseconds through a kernel old timeval into a compat old timeval, reuse the native user stack pointer, use 32-bit uid and gid types, and alias 32-bit signal info copying to the internal helper.

Compat ABI facts here are that 64-bit time use is disabled, the compat minimum signal stack equals the native minimum, bits per compat long derive from the compat long width with a rounding helper, and 64-bit flock packing is architecture selectable including a packed option.

The sanitizer ABI version is five; address, hardware address and thread sanitizer markers and the no-sanitize address attribute expand either to suppression attributes or to nothing depending on toolchain support.

Unsafe compat user-memory helpers require an active user-access region and a caller supplied failure label; use outside such a region or without handling the fault path can mishandle user faults and produce endian-incorrect signal state.
Each generic header in this lane is guarded by an include-once marker preventing repeated inclusion.
